# S238 — Landing merge-in: ork resolves and commits the merge of main itself, and stops the run on conflicts it cannot resolve

*Proposed.* When landing merges the base branch into the slice branch and the merge conflicts, ork's own code resolves what it can (the `CHANGELOG.md` entries), stages and commits the merge and the render itself, and pauses the run with a one-line message that names the remaining files. No role is asked to run `git add` or `git commit`, which roles cannot do. A second owner approval happens only after a red re-check fix round, and `ork status` says so.

**Findings:**  · **Size:** M · **Tree:**

**Not in this slice:**

## Why

Observed on S207's landing (wave 4, 2026-11-02, `.scratch/v11/wave4-friction.md`, F28 and F29; F10 where it concerns the question text). `git merge-tree --write-tree --name-only 3858115 2eb7fc2` (S207's tip and main after S100) reports exactly two conflicts: `CHANGELOG.md` and `internal/registry/registry_test.go`. Verified chain of events:

1. S180's entry-aware resolver was in the running daemon (`0b12869` is an ancestor of the daemon build `b0b1130`), but it never ran on this merge. `resolveChangelog` returns at once unless the unmerged list is exactly `["CHANGELOG.md"]` (`internal/engine/changelog.go:18`), and `TestLandLeavesOtherConflictsToTheFixRound` (`internal/engine/changelog_test.go:130`) pins that. The CHANGELOG conflict itself looks mergeable: each side adds one complete entry at the top of `## Unreleased` (`git diff b0b1130 3858115 -- CHANGELOG.md` and `git diff b0b1130 2eb7fc2 -- CHANGELOG.md`). I did not run the resolver on those stages, so "it would have merged" is not verified.
2. With two files, `mergeBaseIn` called `landBlocked` (`internal/engine/land.go:142-147`), which starts one implementer fix round with the brief `feedbackSection` kind `land` (`internal/engine/states.go:118-123`). That brief tells the role to `git add` the files and run `git commit --no-edit`, and to commit what `slicer render` rewrote.
3. The default implementer allowlist has no `git add` or `git commit` (`internal/engine/perm.go:25-31` lists only `git status`, `git diff`, `git log`), and the design says roles never commit (`docs/design.md:392`, adj 34 `git.commit`). The S207 implementer was Codex `gpt-6.1-sol` (`ork status --json`, roles 4 and 5). Whether Codex's `workspace-write` sandbox also blocks `git` in a linked worktree was never measured (`docs/design.md:829`); the role said it could not. The brief asks for what the allowlist forbids, so the role resolved the files and then asked "Which executor will complete the already-authorized Git staging and commits?". The tests do not catch this: the fake implementer in `internal/engine/land_test.go:576-577` and `internal/engine/changelog_test.go:111-112` runs `git add` and `git commit` itself.
4. The answer "ORK EXECUTOR" only resumes the role (`Engine.Answer`); no ork step commits a conflicted merge. The merge stayed uncommitted, so slicer refused the finish step: `require_no_merge` raises `merge_in_progress` ("Git merge in progress ... finish or abort it", `../slicer/src/slicer/vcs.py:143-150`). `render` and `sync` stay allowed there. A retry of the landing would not have helped either: with `MERGE_HEAD` set, `base` is not an ancestor of `HEAD`, so `mergeBaseIn` runs `git merge` again (`internal/engine/land.go:131-136`), which git refuses.
5. The role's fix round ended, so the run went checks, gate, awaiting approval, and the owner approved a second time. Approve always sets the state to `finish` (`internal/engine/engine.go:404-406`), so the finish step ran again as well; that rerun is outside this slice. `ork status` prints `owner approval` for any awaiting-approval run (`internal/daemon/runs.go:1285`), and nothing in `internal/cli` reads `land_fixes`, so it does not say the approval is a repeat. The TUI has a cue only in the reply to the first `a` (`internal/tui/card.go:671-689`; `docs/dashboard.md:754`).
6. The orchestrator finally committed the merge by hand (`bf6757e`, then a render commit `88c12d3`).

The relay contract already says who takes a conflict a merge driver leaves: the owner (`slicer ai relay`, Land, step 3 on contract v11). ork's role-driven fix round for conflicts is a deviation from that, and `docs/orchestrator-parity.md:90` records it as met. Slicer provides no merge or commit step for ork's landing (`slicer find "merge conflict"` lists only done S119 and the docs re-anchor S219), and landing is ork's (adj 162 `landing.in-ork`).

Adjacent items: S230 item S180(1) (the landing brief still says `stopped on conflicts in: CHANGELOG.md` after a failed merge commit) is removed by this slice, because that brief no longer exists for conflicts. Retire that sub-item when this slice lands.

Owner decisions (interactive question, 2026-11-02): conflicts other than `CHANGELOG.md` go to the owner by hand (no role resolves them); ork resolves `CHANGELOG.md` even when other files conflict; on a retry ork stages the marker-free files, commits the merge, renders and re-checks; the second approval stays only after a red re-check fix round and `ork status` labels it a repeat approval; rerunning the finish step on that approval is a separate slice.

## Implement

The steps follow the owner's answers of 2026-11-02 (see the lead section). Run `rg -n` for each anchor above first; lines move.

1. Tests first, from the lists above. Run them and see the named failures.
2. `internal/engine/landmerge.go`:
   - `mergeInProgress(ctx, dir) bool`: `git -C dir rev-parse -q --verify MERGE_HEAD` succeeds.
   - `hasConflictMarkers(path) bool`: the file has a line that starts `<<<<<<< ` and a line that starts `>>>>>>> ` (a lone `=======` is not a marker; markdown uses it).
   - `settleMerge(ctx, rec, base) (done bool, err error)`: read `git diff --name-only --diff-filter=U`. (a) If `CHANGELOG.md` is listed and still has markers, call `resolveChangelog`. (b) For each remaining file that exists and has no markers, `git add -- FILE`. Never `git add -A` and never `git add .`. (c) Read the unmerged list again; if any remain, pause with `conflictReason` and return `false, thatError`. (d) Otherwise `git commit -m "Merge BASE into BRANCH"`; a failure pauses with `git commit: ` plus git's message. Return `true, nil`.
   - `conflictReason(base, branch, worktree, runID string, files []string) string`: one line, at most five names then `+N more`, the worktree path, and `resolve them there (no need to git add), then ork retry RUN; ork commits the merge`. Pause with `runrec.Pending{Kind: runrec.PendingError, State: runrec.StateLand, Reason: ...}`. The run is paused, not stopped, so `ork retry` and `t` work.
3. `internal/engine/changelog.go`: `resolveChangelog` writes the merged file and `git add -- CHANGELOG.md` (keep `writeChangelog` and its marker restore on failure), and no longer commits. It still returns `false, nil` when a stage is missing or `mergeChangelogEntries` refuses. Remove the `len(unmerged) != 1` guard; the caller passes only `CHANGELOG.md`. Keep the name check: only the root `CHANGELOG.md`.
4. `internal/engine/land.go`, `mergeBaseIn`: before `git merge`, if `!has` and `mergeInProgress(W)`, call `settleMerge` and return its failure; otherwise run `git merge` as now and, when it fails with unmerged files, call `settleMerge`. A failure with no unmerged files (for example an untracked file in the way) pauses with git's message as today (`land.go:149-151`). Remove the `landBlocked(ctx, "merge conflict", ...)` call. The render, commit-what-render-rewrote and re-check code (`land.go:154-177`) is unchanged and runs after a settled merge; `LandRecheck` handling is unchanged. `landBlocked` stays for the red re-check (`land.go:173-177`).
5. `internal/engine/states.go:118-123`: rewrite the `land` brief for the red re-check only: ork merged the base branch into the branch, rendered and committed; the checks are red; fix them (for example a golden another slice changed); do not commit, rebase, force, reset or abort; the gate runs again and the owner approves again. Say in the report what changed.
6. Status text: `source.EngineRun.LandFixes`, filled in `internal/daemon/runs.go:1342` from `rec.LandFixes`. In `internal/cli/daemoncmds.go:85-87`, when `r.State == "awaiting-approval"` and `r.LandFixes > 0`, print `(wait: owner approval, again: the landing was blocked and its fix round is done)`. Leave the daemon's `wait` string (`runs.go:1285`) as `owner approval`, because the TUI hides exactly that text (`internal/tui/overview.go:1544`). Do not touch `internal/tui`.
7. Docs, as listed in Files. Mark everything beyond the roadmap *proposed*. Do not paste the relay contract's text; refer to `slicer ai relay`.
8. Do not touch: `internal/engine/perm.go` (the allowlist stays as it is), `internal/tui`, the finish step, `Approve`, or any slicer or adj data. Do not run `git merge --abort`, `git reset` or `--force` anywhere.
10. Add the CHANGELOG entry last, as the first item under `## Unreleased`, marked *proposed*.
